Archetype: B (Quality Compounder) — with a D (Product-Platform) overlay
           on the membership-fee stream. Primary engine: Engine 1

DATA-QUALITY FLAG (material):

SECTION 1. MACRO CONTEXT

  Judgment: NEUTRAL-to-HEADWIND.
  Conviction adjustment: −0.5 step (headwind). The high multiple

  stagflation regime with a 4.7%+ 10-yr and a holding Fed provides

SECTION 1.5. BASE RATE CHECK
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Step 1.5-1. Similar-enterprise base rates:
  • 5-year survival of a Quality Compounder (Archetype B): ~95%+
    (Costco has survived 60+ years; base rate is very high).
  • Probability a 47x-P/E quality compounder delivers >15% CAGR
    over the next 5 years: ~25-35% (base rate for high-multiple
    quality names; the multiple already prices in steady growth).
  • Actual reach rate for "steady 8-10% revenue growth for a
    decade" at this scale ($300B+): ~40-50% (large retailers
    decelerate; Costco's membership model is a genuine differentiator).
  • Base rate for a 47x-P/E name to re-rate UP (not down) over
    3 years absent a multiple expansion: ~20-30%.

Step 1.5-2. Deviation of current analysis from base rate:
  My base-case DCF IV ($440) is ~53% BELOW the T0 price ($947.74).
  This is a LARGE deviation from the "fair value ≈ price" prior.
  Three company-specific justifications for why the market might
  be right and my DCF conservative:
    1. The membership-fee stream (~$5.3B/yr, ~90% margin, 90%+
       renewal) is a genuine recurring-revenue asset that a simple
       FCF DCF under-weights; it behaves like a subscription.
    2. The working-capital source (deferred fees + payables) is a
       structural, recurring benefit that boosts FCF beyond a
       naive NOPAT+D&A−capex model.
    3. The ROIC is ~37% [Estimate] (net cash, high NOPAT), which
       justifies a premium multiple vs. a typical retailer.
  However, these justifications do NOT close a 53% gap. They
  justify a PREMIUM to a typical retailer, not a 2x premium to
  my base-case DCF. The deviation is therefore PARTIALLY
  justified but NOT fully. I keep the base-case DCF and carry the
  gap into the scenarios.

Step 1.5-3. Base-rate shock check:
  My "success probability" (that the stock is fairly valued at
  $947.74) is well below 1.5x the base rate for a 47x-P/E name
  to be fairly valued. No red flag. The concern is the opposite:
  the PRICE is above my DCF, not the other way around.

SECTION 2. BUSINESS QUALITY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Step 2-1. Business understanding (3 sentences):
  Costco is a membership-based wholesale club retailer that sells
  a curated, bulk, low-margin merchandise assortment to ~130M+
  paying members, earning a structurally low merchandise margin
  (~2-3%) and a high-margin recurring membership fee (~$5.3B/yr,
  ~90% margin). It operates 931 warehouses across 15 countries
  [Actual, Q3 FY2026 press release] plus e-commerce in 9 markets.
  Profit is driven by membership renewal (90.2% global, 92.7%
  US-Canada [Actual]) and scale-driven supply-chain efficiency,
  not by merchandise markup.
  Understandability: HIGH.

Step 2-2. Moat assessment (0-3 each) + direction:
  Intangible assets (brand):        3  — Stable (strong, trusted brand)
  Switching costs:                  2  — Stable (annual commitment,
                                          bulk shopping habit; not
                                          high but real)
  Network effects:                  1  — Stable (weak; not a two-sided
                                          network in the tech sense)
  Cost advantage:                   3  — Widening (scale, no
                                          advertising spend, direct
                                          vendor relationships,

  Economies of scale:               3  — Widening (931 warehouses,

  Regulatory barriers:              1  — Stable (low; retail is not

  Data moat:                        1  — Stable (membership data is

  MOAT SCORE: 14/21 → WIDE MOAT.
  Moat direction: STABLE-to-WIDENING on cost/scale; STABLE on
  brand/switching. No narrowing signals detected. The main moat
  risk is competitive (Walmart/Amazon) and macro (consumer
  spending), not structural.

Step 2-3. Lynch classification:
  STALWART (large, well-established, steady grower). Core
  checkpoints:
  • Growing earnings at a steady clip: YES (EPS +10.2% consensus
    [Estimate]; net income CAGR ~10% over 5y [Actual]).
  • Conservative financial policies: YES (net cash, low leverage).
  • Reasonable valuation: NO (47.9x trailing P/E is NOT

Step 2-4. Financial strength scorecard:

  3. Capex efficiency: 3 — incremental ROIC on warehouse

SECTION 2.5. INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Step 2.5-1. R&D capitalization:
  Costco has minimal R&D (not a material line item). Not
  applicable. Adjusted OI ≈ reported OI.

Step 2.5-2. SBC proper treatment:
  SBC FY2025: $0.860B [Actual]. Adjusted FCF = reported FCF − SBC
  = $7.837B − $0.860B = $6.977B [Estimate]. SBC is ~0.31% of
  revenue and ~10% of net income — a real but modest economic
  cost. Share count is stable (net issuance ~0% [Actual]), so
  dilution is minimal.

Step 2.5-3. Operating lease capitalization:
  Operating leases FY2025: $2.668B [Actual]. These are warehouse
  leases. Adding them to debt: total debt = $7.267B + $2.668B =
  $9.935B. Net debt = $9.935B − $15.284B = −$5.349B (still net
  cash). The conclusion (net cash) is unchanged.

Step 2.5-4. Brand/data asset estimation:
  Brand: Costco's brand is strong but not a consumer-goods brand
  in the Interbrand sense; it is a retail brand. Value is
  embedded in the membership base. Not separately capitalized.
  Data: membership data is valuable but not a compounding data
  asset. Not separately capitalized.

Step 2.5-5. Adjusted ROIC:
  Adjusted NOPAT = reported NOPAT (no R&D adjustment) = $7.79B.
  Adjusted IC = $21.15B (no R&D adjustment).
  Adjusted ROIC = 7.79/21.15 = 36.8% [Estimate].
  Gap vs GAAP ROIC: minimal (no R&D to capitalize). The high ROIC
  is driven by the net-cash position and the membership-fee
  margin, not by intangible capitalization.

Step 2.5-6. Owner earnings (Buffett style):
  Owner earnings = Net income + D&A − maintenance capex − ΔWC.
  Net income FY2025: $8.099B [Actual]
  D&A FY2025: $2.426B [Actual]
  Maintenance capex: ~40% of total capex = ~$2.20B [Assumption]
  ΔWC: ~−$2.0B (a source of cash; deferred fees + payables)
         [Estimate, backed out from OCF]
  Owner earnings ≈ 8.099 + 2.426 − 2.20 + 2.0 = $10.3B [Estimate]
  Owner-earnings multiple at T0: $420.3B / $10.3B = 40.8x
  [Estimate]. This is a HIGH multiple, confirming the stock is
  priced for quality, not value.

SECTION 3.5. SECOND-ORDER EFFECTS

  Positive: High stock price → talent attraction (SBC), M&A

  Negative: Low stock price → talent drain, member concern

Step 3.5-3. Customer behavior evolution:
  Early adopter → mainstream: Costco is already mainstream

  membership fees are rising ($65 Gold Star, $130 Executive

Step 4.5-2. My horizon vs market horizon:

  Spread = 10 − 6 (midpoint of market implied) = 4 years.

  HOWEVER: the arbitrage is NOT actionable at T0 because the
  market's shorter-horizon pricing is ALREADY reflected in the
  high multiple. The "arbitrage" would be to SELL (the market is
  overpaying for the long-horizon growth), not to buy.
  Net: The horizon spread argues for a SELL/AVOID, not a buy.

  2. Valuation attractiveness: 0 (47.9x P/E, 60x P/FCF, NO
